Sampled HR@10 and full-catalog ranking measure different candidate conditions. RecSys 2025 finds negative-sampling strategies affect model separability, agreement with full evaluation, and robustness to exposure bias; 2024 sequential-recommendation experiments find random negative sampling favors head items. Consequently, preserve the pinned 99-negative validation protocol for selection; report popularity-matched and model-hard candidate probes separately as diagnostic stress tests. Stratify hits and target ranks by training-only item popularity and history length, including subgroup counts. [Sampling reliability, 2025](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086); [negative-sampling experiments, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276).

Embedding spectra provide information that mean cosine misses. ICML 2024 identifies recommendation embedding collapse into low-dimensional subspaces; the 2026 SpecFormer preprint also examines embedding and attention collapse. A useful diagnostic proposal is entropy effective rank, exp(−Σpᵢ log pᵢ), with pᵢ equal to normalized singular values: report matrix centering, sampled rows, singular spectrum, and embedding norms, excluding padding/mask tokens. Low effective rank signals restricted representation capacity, but does not establish poor HR@10 by itself. [Embedding collapse, 2024](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/guo24e.html); [SpecFormer, 2026 preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24025).

For this benchmark, bootstrap users within each category and recompute the four-category macro average; use paired user resampling for model differences with fixed candidates. These intervals describe evaluation-user uncertainty, not training-seed or candidate-sampling uncertainty. No located evidence establishes that inexpensive training-prefix probes predict this benchmark’s validation HR@10: measure that agreement across trials, label in-sample optimism, and retain the fixed splits. Keep full-catalog coverage/popularity diagnostics separate, preserve one BERT4Rec checkpoint per category, and never fuse diagnostic scores into predictions.
